text:
priya: Quick brain dump from customer calls: three customers asked for burst carryover (unused burst minutes roll into next day) and one asked for smoother throttles instead of hard 429s. Can we design an "adaptive smoothing" approach?

tess: I like carryover but worried about cost. Propose param: carryover_enabled true/false, carryover_cap_percent (0-50%), and decay window (hours). That caps risk.

noah: Runtime idea: smoothing uses a leaky-bucket fed by commit and burst credits. When demand spikes, tokens are drawn from the bucket; if depleted, apply progressive soft-throttle (increase latency by weighted queue) before hard reject. Need to define weights.

li: Ops constraints: queueing increases memory/latency and can cause head-of-line blocking. We can implement short time-slicing: max_queue_ms per request (e.g., 200ms) and progressive backoff steps (200ms, 400ms, 800ms). Also must instrument queue depth and per-tenant queued_ms.

carlos: Billing: customers hate surprise fractional dollars. Suggest we round burst usage to nearest minute and display a running invoice estimate in the console. For carryover, bill only for actual overage, not for carried credit.

billing-bot: Note: backend currently records burst_usage_seconds and bills per token-minute. We'll need an aggregation transform if we switch to minute rounding.

priya: UX: show two new numbers: "burst_balance" (minutes available today) and "carryover_available" (minutes carried). Also add tooltip explaining decay rules.

noah: Algorithm specifics proposal:
- bucket_capacity = commit_minutes * (1 + burst_headroom_pct) + carryover_minutes
- refill_rate = commit_minutes / day
- smoothing_window = 60s sliding decay for immediate burst smoothing
- soft_throttle_curve: latency_penalty = base * (1 + alpha * deficit_fraction) up to max_queue_ms

li: Observability: emit metrics per tenant: bucket_level, queue_depth, avg_queue_ms, soft_throttle_events, hard_throttle_count. Add alert when hard_throttle_count > 5 in 1m.

tess: Legal/sales ask: define default carryover = 0 for self-serve, 10% for enterprise with explicit opt-in. Document in SLA: carryover not guaranteed in extreme load and can be reclaimed if cluster pressure > 90%.

carlos: Implementation notes: rounding change needs migration. We'll show two invoice lines for first month (legacy rounding + new rounding) during pilot to avoid disputes.

priya: Pilot plan: 2 pilot customers, enable carryover opt-in, smoothing enabled for all. Measure: p95 latency under smoothing <= baseline + 50ms during 95% of spikes, and billing disputes <= 1 per pilot.

noah: Rollout plan:
- week 1: spec + playbook + metric schema
- week 2: implement bucket + soft-throttle in runtime (feature flag)
- week 3: console UX + billing rounding pipeline
- week 4: pilot with canary pool, run synthetic spikes

li: Danger: if carryover + elastic burst combined could allow runaway usage. We should enforce a daily hard cap = commit_minutes * (1 + global_max_burst) regardless of carryover.

priya: Agreed. Default global_max_burst = 50% of commit for pilot.

tess: Copy for console microcopy: "Burst minutes are temporary headroom tied to your reserved pool. Carryover saves a portion of unused minutes to the next day; it is subject to cluster capacity and may be reclaimed during high demand."

carlos: Billing FAQ entry: "Why was I billed for a minute I thought was carried?" -> explain decay & reclaimed cases and provide dispute contact.

priya: Acceptance criteria for pilot:
- metrics emitted and dashboards created
- smoothing reduces hard 429s by >=60% in synthetic tests
- billing pipeline shows minute-rounded usage and invoice preview in console
- carryover toggle in API + console works and respects caps

billing-bot: Reminder: add audit log entries when carryover granted/reclaimed.

noah: Tech risk list: queue overhead, edge-case fairness across tenants, billing migration complexity. We'll document mitigations in the RFC.

priya: Actions: noah to draft RFC (due Tue), tess to mock console (Wed), li to add metrics + alert stubs (Thu), carlos to draft billing FAQ & invoice preview text (Fri).

priya: Thanks all. We'll review RFC + mocks before enabling pilot. :rocket:
